commit_message:
POP3: fix multi-line responses

Some POP3 commands are multi-line, e.g. have responses terminated by a
last line with '.', but some are not. Define the known command
properties and fix response handling.

Add test case for STAT.

Fixes #14677
Reported-by: ralfjunker on github
Closes #14707

diff --git a/lib/pop3.c b/lib/pop3.c
index 47271252e8..1d12a71632 100644
--- a/lib/pop3.c
+++ b/lib/pop3.c
@@ -81,10 +81,14 @@
 /* The last 3 #include files should be in this order */
 #include "curl_printf.h"
 #include "curl_memory.h"
 #include "memdebug.h"
 
+#ifndef ARRAYSIZE
+#define ARRAYSIZE(A) (sizeof(A)/sizeof((A)[0]))
+#endif
+
 /* Local API functions */
 static CURLcode pop3_regular_transfer(struct Curl_easy *data, bool *done);
 static CURLcode pop3_do(struct Curl_easy *data, bool *done);
 static CURLcode pop3_done(struct Curl_easy *data, CURLcode status,
                           bool premature);
@@ -197,10 +201,57 @@ static void pop3_to_pop3s(struct connectdata *conn)
 }
 #else
 #define pop3_to_pop3s(x) Curl_nop_stmt
 #endif
 
+struct pop3_cmd {
+  const char *name;
+  unsigned short nlen;
+  BIT(multiline); /* response is multi-line with last '.' line */
+  BIT(multiline_with_args); /* is multi-line when command has args */
+};
+
+static const struct pop3_cmd pop3cmds[] = {
+  { "APOP", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "AUTH", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "CAPA", 4, TRUE, TRUE },
+  { "DELE", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "LIST", 4, TRUE, TRUE },
+  { "MSG",  3, TRUE, TRUE },
+  { "NOOP", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "PASS", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "QUIT", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "RETR", 4, TRUE, TRUE },
+  { "RSET", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "STAT", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "STLS", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "TOP",  3, TRUE, TRUE },
+  { "UIDL", 4, TRUE, FALSE },
+  { "USER", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "UTF8", 4, FALSE, FALSE },
+  { "XTND", 4, TRUE, TRUE },
+};
+
+/* Return iff a command is defined as "multi-line" (RFC 1939),
+ * has a response terminated by a last line with a '.'.
+ */
+static bool pop3_is_multiline(const char *cmdline)
+{
+  size_t i;
+  for(i = 0; i < ARRAYSIZE(pop3cmds); ++i) {
+    if(strncasecompare(pop3cmds[i].name, cmdline, pop3cmds[i].nlen)) {
+      if(!cmdline[pop3cmds[i].nlen])
+        return pop3cmds[i].multiline;
+      else if(cmdline[pop3cmds[i].nlen] == ' ')
+        return pop3cmds[i].multiline_with_args;
+    }
+  }
+  /* Unknown command, assume multi-line for backward compatibility with
+   * earlier curl versions that only could do multi-line responses. */
+  return TRUE;
+}
+

  * Checks for an ending POP3 status code at the start of the given string, but
@@ -612,22 +663,24 @@ static CURLcode pop3_perform_command(struct Curl_easy *data)
       pop3->transfer = PPTRANSFER_INFO;
   }
   else
     command = "RETR";
 
+  if(pop3->custom && pop3->custom[0] != '\0')

+
   /* Send the command */
   if(pop3->id[0] != '\0')
     result = Curl_pp_sendf(data, &conn->proto.pop3c.pp, "%s %s",
-                           (pop3->custom && pop3->custom[0] != '\0' ?
-                            pop3->custom : command), pop3->id);
+                           command, pop3->id);
   else
-    result = Curl_pp_sendf(data, &conn->proto.pop3c.pp, "%s",
-                           (pop3->custom && pop3->custom[0] != '\0' ?
-                            pop3->custom : command));
+    result = Curl_pp_sendf(data, &conn->proto.pop3c.pp, "%s", command);
 
-  if(!result)
+  if(!result) {
     pop3_state(data, POP3_COMMAND);
+    data->req.no_body = !pop3_is_multiline(command);
+  }
 
   return result;

fix_commit.message: pop3: function could get the ->transfer field wrong
fix_commit.author: Daniel Stenberg

findings.title: pop3_perform() reads stale data->req.no_body before pop3_perform_command() recomputes it
findings.message: Commit 4cd10ee28b introduced logic in pop3_perform_command() that recomputes data->req.no_body based on whether the outgoing POP3 command is multi-line (data->req.no_body = !pop3_is_multiline(command);). However, pop3_perform() (the caller) reads data->req.no_body BEFORE calling pop3_perform_command(), using its value (set previously, e.g. from a prior request or left over from handle state) to decide whether pop3->transfer should be set to PPTRANSFER_INFO (no body transfer expected). Because pop3_perform_command() only updates data->req.no_body afterwards, pop3->transfer can end up reflecting the OLD no_body value instead of the value that was just computed for the current command. This means the transfer state machine can incorrectly believe a body transfer is or is not expected, causing curl to mishandle the POP3 response (e.g. treat data as headers-only when a body should be read, or vice versa), leading to incorrect state handling / data corruption for POP3 transfers, particularly across handle reuse where req.no_body carries over from an earlier request.
findings.suggestion: Reorder pop3_perform() so it calls pop3_perform_command() first (which computes the correct, up-to-date data->req.no_body for the current command), and only afterwards check data->req.no_body to decide whether pop3->transfer should be set to PPTRANSFER_INFO. This is exactly what the upstream fix (commit 67c4256f7e) does: it moves the pop3_perform_command() call before the data->req.no_body check in pop3_perform().

ground_truth.root_cause: A caller (pop3_perform) read a shared state field (data->req.no_body) to make a decision, while the callee it subsequently invokes (pop3_perform_command) is the one responsible for computing/updating that same field for the current operation. The call order was wrong: the read-and-decide step happened before the compute step, so decisions were based on stale state.
